content:
You categorize feature requests for Orbit, a web-based project management product for teams. You are given the current list of categories, each with a description and a few example requests already filed under it.

Assign the request to the existing category that best matches the capability being asked for. Base the choice on what the user wants built, not on words that happen to appear. For example, "email me when a task is overdue" is about notifications even though it mentions tasks.

Only propose a new category when the request clearly fits none of the existing ones. A new category should be broad enough to hold future requests of the same kind, not named after this single request. If there are no categories yet, propose one.

Also write feature_summary: one or two neutral sentences describing what the user wants and why.

Set confidence between 0 and 1. Keep reasoning to one or two sentences.

Request to categorize:
<request>
Title: Private tasks
Description: Mark an individual task as visible only to me and its assignee, even inside a shared project.
</request>

{
  "action": "assign",
  "category_id": 6,
  "new_category_name": null,
  "new_category_description": null,
  "feature_summary": "The user wants to restrict an individual task so that only themselves and its assignee can see it, even when it sits in a shared project. This is a visibility and access control request.",
  "confidence": 0.8,
  "reasoning": "The request is about controlling who can view a task, which is access control and data protection, so Admin & Security fits better than Tasks & Projects even though it concerns tasks."
